newsitem.title: UK: China boosts armed forces but range limited - study.
newsitem.headline: China boosts armed forces but range limited - study.

text.p: China is making significant efforts to improve the effectiveness of its huge armed forces but faces major problems operating beyond its borders, the International Institute for Strategic Affairs (IISS) said on Wednesday.
"China is continuing its attempts to make qualitative improvements in its nuclear and conventional combat capability," the IISS said in its annual report on the state of the world's armed forces.
The Chinese armed forces number 2.9 million, by far the largest in the world, although the IISS said Beijing was planning to cut the total by 500,000.

"All these efforts reinforce the trend away from wide-area territorial defence to manoeuvre formations that can be moved rapidly to deal with a serious domestic emergency or an external threat to China's territorial integrity," it said.

The IISS put China's 1995 military spending at $32 billion, far above the official armed forces budget of around $7.7 billion, and said higher procurement charges were likely to help push the real 1996 figure much higher.

China, which in late July exploded its 45th nuclear device since 1964, was working closely with Russia and other countries to improve its conventional forces and earn enough money to fund its defence programme, the report said.

"The Peoples' Liberation Army is improving the mobility of at least six high-quality mobile formations, the so-called "Fist' divisions, and to this end it carried out a major logistic exercise in south-west China in July 1998."
But serious shortcomings in both the navy and air force meant China would find it hard to mount a major operation far beyond its borders, the report predicted.
The navy -- "its warships are no match for the more modern navies in the region" -- did not have the capability to transport troops and heavy weapons for long distances.
"The poor air-defence and anti-submarine capabilities of China's major warships also means the navy lacks the capability to provide adequate protection for an amphibious force," the report said.
"Because of virtually non-existent air-to-air refuelling capability, the Chinese air force could not provide continuous air support at extended range from mainland bases," it added.

Although Russia continued to be China's main source of modern weapon systems and military technology, Moscow would probably show some caution in future given Beijing's links with Pakistan, Iran and Israel, the report said.
